\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{انتقال} \ur{کرنا} (intiqāl karnā)}{انتقال کرنا (intiqāl karnā)}]{\ur{انتقال} \ur{کرنا} (intiqāl karnā) — to pass away}

\label{lesson:UR-C493-intiqal-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a last will, then the Urdu for an inheritance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{انتقال} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{انتقال} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{intiqāl karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to pass away\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دادا} \ur{پچھلے} \ur{سال} \ur{انتقال} \ur{کر} \ur{گئے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādā pichhle sāl intiqāl kar gae.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather passed away last year.
\end{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{انتقال} \ur{کر} \ur{گئی}, \emph{voh intiqāl kar gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{انتقال} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{intiqāl karnā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{انتقال}}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{intiqāl}, \textquotedblleft{}moving from one place to another\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intiqāl karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intiqāl karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādā pichhle sāl intiqāl kar gae.} — My grandfather passed away last year.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a last will, then the Urdu for an inheritance, then say \emph{intiqāl karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{انتقال} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To pass away\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جنازہ} (janāzā)}{جنازہ (janāzā)}]{\ur{جنازہ} (janāzā) — a funeral}

\label{lesson:UR-C493-janaza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an inheritance, then the Urdu for to pass away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جنازہ}}
\textbf{\ur{جنازہ}} — \emph{janāzā} — \textquotedblleft{}a funeral\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{جنازے} \ur{میں} \ur{سب} \ur{رشتہ} \ur{دار} \ur{آئے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{janāze meṅ sab rishte dār āe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
All the relatives came to the funeral.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جنازہ}} (\emph{janāzā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{janāza}, \textquotedblleft{}a bier, a funeral\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{janāze meṅ sab rishte dār āe.} — All the relatives came to the funeral.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for an inheritance, then the Urdu for to pass away, then say \emph{janāzā} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دفنانا} (dafnānā)}{دفنانا (dafnānā)}]{\ur{دفنانا} (dafnānā) — to bury the dead}

\label{lesson:UR-C493-dafnana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to pass away, then the Urdu for a funeral.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دفنانا}}
\textbf{\ur{دفنانا}} — \emph{dafnānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to bury the dead\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{انہوں} \ur{نے} \ur{دادا} \ur{کو} \ur{قبرستان} \ur{میں} \ur{دفنایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{unhoṅ ne dādā ko qabristān meṅ dafnāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They buried my grandfather in the graveyard.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{پرندے} \ur{کو} \ur{دفنایا}, \emph{us ne parinde ko dafnāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دفنانا}} (\emph{dafnānā}) is built on \emph{dafn}, \textquotedblleft{}burial\textquotedblright{}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{dafn}, made into an Urdu verb with \emph{-ānā}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to pass away, then the Urdu for a funeral, then say \emph{dafnānā} again
\end{itemize}

\label{lesson:UR-C493-beva}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to bury the dead, then the Urdu for to offer condolences.

\textbf{\ur{بیوہ}} — \emph{bevā} — \textquotedblleft{}a widow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{بیوہ} \ur{اپنے} \ur{بیٹے} \ur{کو} \ur{اکیلی} \ur{پالتی} \ur{ہے۔}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh bevā apne beṭe ko akelī pāltī hai.}

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from A Wedding to Mourning}

\label{lesson:UR-R493-review-487-493}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for an engagement to marry and the marriage contract.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item an engagement to marry, the marriage contract, the wedding procession, a bridegroom's veil of flowers, to see off
  \item a wedding feast, the in-laws' home, a daughter-in-law, a son-in-law, to marry off
  \item a husband's younger brother, a husband's elder brother, a husband's sister, a nephew (a sister's son), a grandson (a daughter's son)
  \item a father's elder brother, a mother's sister's husband, related by remarriage, an orphan, to adopt
  \item ill feeling, a grievance, a taunt, a divorce, to forgive
  \item old age, the power to remember, a walking stick, a last will, an inheritance
  \item to pass away, a funeral, to bury the dead, to offer condolences, a widow
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
An engagement to marry? (\textbf{\ur{منگنی}}, \emph{mangnī}.) The marriage contract? (\textbf{\ur{نکاح}}, \emph{nikāh}.) The wedding procession? (\textbf{\ur{بارات}}, \emph{bārāt}.) A bridegroom's veil of flowers? (\textbf{\ur{سہرا}}, \emph{sehrā}.) To see off? (\textbf{\ur{رخصت} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{rukhsat karnā}.) A wedding feast? (\textbf{\ur{ولیمہ}}, \emph{valīmā}.) The in-laws' home? (\textbf{\ur{سسرال}}, \emph{susrāl}.) A daughter-in-law? (\textbf{\ur{بہو}}, \emph{bahū}.) A son-in-law? (\textbf{\ur{داماد}}, \emph{dāmād}.) To marry off? (\textbf{\ur{بیاہنا}}, \emph{byāhnā}.) A husband's younger brother? (\textbf{\ur{دیور}}, \emph{devar}.) A husband's elder brother? (\textbf{\ur{جیٹھ}}, \emph{jeṭh}.) A husband's sister? (\textbf{\ur{نند}}, \emph{nanad}.) A nephew (a sister's son)? (\textbf{\ur{بھانجا}}, \emph{bhāṅjā}.) A grandson (a daughter's son)? (\textbf{\ur{نواسا}}, \emph{navāsā}.) A father's elder brother? (\textbf{\ur{تایا}}, \emph{tāyā}.) A mother's sister's husband? (\textbf{\ur{خالو}}, \emph{khālū}.) Related by remarriage? (\textbf{\ur{سوتیلا}}, \emph{sautelā}.) An orphan? (\textbf{\ur{یتیم}}, \emph{yatīm}.) To adopt? (\textbf{\ur{گود} \ur{لینا}}, \emph{god lenā}.) Ill feeling? (\textbf{\ur{رنجش}}, \emph{ranjish}.) A grievance? (\textbf{\ur{شکوہ}}, \emph{shikvā}.) A taunt? (\textbf{\ur{طعنہ}}, \emph{tānā}.) A divorce? (\textbf{\ur{طلاق}}, \emph{talāq}.) To forgive? (\textbf{\ur{معاف} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{māf karnā}.) Old age? (\textbf{\ur{بڑھاپا}}, \emph{buṛhāpā}.) The power to remember? (\textbf{\ur{یادداشت}}, \emph{yāddāsht}.) A walking stick? (\textbf{\ur{چھڑی}}, \emph{chhaṛī}.) A last will? (\textbf{\ur{وصیت}}, \emph{vasiyat}.) An inheritance? (\textbf{\ur{وراثت}}, \emph{virāsat}.) To pass away? (\textbf{\ur{انتقال} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{intiqāl karnā}.) A funeral? (\textbf{\ur{جنازہ}}, \emph{janāzā}.) To bury the dead? (\textbf{\ur{دفنانا}}, \emph{dafnānā}.) To offer condolences? (\textbf{\ur{تعزیت} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{tāziyat karnā}.) A widow? (\textbf{\ur{بیوہ}}, \emph{bevā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
